title: Build one route table from every round

blocks.text: The HTTP server reads its route table from `practice.generated.Routes`, which `RouteIndexProcessor` writes at compile time from every class marked `@Route("/path")`. The team has just added a client generator to the build: another annotation processor that writes handler classes of its own, also marked `@Route`. Since then the route table has been the problem.

Finish `record(...)` and `timeToWrite(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/RouteIndexProcessor.java`. Both are called on every call of `process`. The table must list every handler of the build, the ones in the sources and the ones other processors generate, and writing it must never fail the build. About four lines in total.
The tests compile handler classes with `javax.tools.JavaCompiler`, your processor, and a stand-in for the client generator.

cases.says: with handlers only in the sources, the build passes and the table maps each path to its handler class
a handler generated by another processor, a round after the sources, doesn't make writing the table fail
a handler generated by another processor is in the table along with the handlers in the sources

origin.section: The Filer Creates Each File Once and Never Replaces a Class That Exists

concepts: The Filer creates a file once per compile, so an aggregate file written in every round with annotations fails with FilerException once a later round brings more; collecting across rounds and writing once fixes it.
A processor runs inside javac, reads declarations through javax.lang.model rather than Class objects, and adds new source files through the Filer that are compiled with the sources.
